extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, attorneys/agents, and third‑party requesters preparing or evaluating ex parte reexamination requests
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and filing an ex parte reexamination request under 35 U.S.C. 302 and 37 CFR 1.510, including format, content, fees, service, and standards for a 'substantial new question of patentability.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative authority (37 CFR 1.34 / 1.32(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: To act in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 an attorney or agent must set forth registration number, name, and signature; to act under a power of attorney the requester must provide a power of attorney and the representative must be an inventor or a registered patent practitioner (37 CFR 1.32(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any question of authority arises, proof of authority may be required. All correspondence for a requester that is not the patent owner is addressed to the representative unless specifically indicated otherwise. A patent owner may not be represented by an unregistered person in reexamination since 37 CFR 1.33(c) prohibits signing amendments and other papers by unregistered persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment requirement (37 CFR 1.510(a) / 1.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for ex parte reexamination must be accompanied by the appropriate fee for requesting reexamination as specified in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) or (c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request by the patent owner includes a proposed amendment under 37 CFR 1.530, excess claims fees under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) may apply. If the fee is missing or other filing requirements incomplete, the requester will be notified and given an opportunity to complete; failure to comply generally results in no filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of each substantial new question of patentability (37 CFR 1.510(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should clearly point out what the requester considers to be the substantial new question of patentability which would warrant a reexamination. The cited prior art should be listed on form PTO/SB/08 or PTO/SB/42 (or an equivalent format). A requester must assert how the cited documents raise a substantial new question of patentability; the requester must not argue that submitted references do not raise a substantial new question and that no reexamination should be ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of every claim and detailed explanation of pertinency (37 CFR 1.510(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of every claim for which reexamination is requested and a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to every claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each patent owner statement submitted under 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2) that is relied upon, the request must explain how that statement is used to determine the proper meaning of a claim in connection with the prior art applied to that claim and how each relevant claim is being interpreted. The requester may point out how claims distinguish over cited prior art. The Office will consider these explanations during examination; at the order stage the Office will not consider patent owner claim scope statements referenced in the request (see 35 U.S.C. 301(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of every relied-upon patent or printed publication and translations (37 CFR 1.510(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon or referred to in the request, accompanied by an English translation of necessary and pertinent parts of any non-English document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A listing of patents and printed publications as provided for in 37 CFR 1.98 must be provided. A comprehensive listing and submission is required so materials are available for examiner consideration. Submission of copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications is waived to the extent they are not required by the Office; see MPEP § 2218.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the entire patent for which reexamination is requested (37 CFR 1.510(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the entire patent including the front face, drawings, and specification/claims (in double column format) and of any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or reexamination certificate issued in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All copies must have each page plainly written on only one side of a sheet of paper. The printed patent reproduced as it appears (front page, drawings, abstract, specification, claims) may be used; two‑sided copies are not proper. Any disclaimer/corrections become part of the patent and must be supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of service on patent owner (37 CFR 1.510(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification that a copy of the request filed by a person other than the patent owner has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the address provided in 37 CFR 1.33(c); the name and address of the party served must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service was not possible after reasonable effort, a duplicate copy must be supplied to the Office with a cover letter explaining efforts made and why service failed. Requesters are encouraged to clearly label a duplicate filing to avoid erroneous duplicate filing fee charges. Service details should be complete because the requester’s submission may be the only opportunity to participate if the patent owner does not file a statement under 37 CFR 1.530(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel certification by third-party requester (37 CFR 1.510(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification by the third-party requester that statutory estoppel provisions of 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) or 35 U.S.C. 325(e)(1) do not prohibit the requester from filing the ex parte reexamination request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures compliance with estoppel provisions from inter partes review and post-grant review. Rules do not require requesters to identify themselves; a real party in interest may remain anonymous by using a registered practitioner who will certify the requester is not estopped. An individual filing on their own behalf cannot remain anonymous because they must sign the certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements (completeness and OCR reproducibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a reexamination filing date, request papers must satisfy all requirements of 37 CFR 1.510(a) and (b), be accompanied by the appropriate fee, and meet the clarity/contrast requirements enabling direct reproduction and OCR capture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests that fail to meet requirements or lack fees will not be granted a filing date unless defects are cured. Requests not granted a filing date may be placed in the patent file as a citation under 37 CFR 1.501 if they comply with 1.501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined reduced-fee eligibility (37 CFR 1.20(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests filed on/after Jan 16, 2018 may use a reduced filing fee under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) if they comply with all requirements of 1.20(c)(1) and 37 CFR 1.510(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for the reduced fee include: (1) forty (40) or fewer pages; (2) double-spaced or one-and-a-half spaced lines; (3) non-script font such as Arial, Times New Roman, or Courier; (4) font size no smaller than 12 point; (5) margins conforming to 37 CFR 1.52(a)(1)(ii); and (6) sufficient clarity/contrast for direct reproduction and OCR. The reduced-fee option affects only the filing fee, not subsequent reexamination processing or priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts excluded from the streamlined page/format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain parts of an ex parte reexamination request are excluded from the page/format limits of 1.20(c)(1)(i)(A)-(E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded parts: (a) copies of every patent or printed publication relied upon (1.510(b)(3)); (b) the copy of the entire patent for which reexamination is requested (1.510(b)(4)); (c) the certifications required by 1.510(b)(5) and (6); and (d) completed forms such as PTO/SB/57 or the information disclosure statement form (PTO/SB/08) or equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-count inclusion for claim charts and argumentative papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim charts are considered part of the request and are included in the page limit; other papers submitted with or as part of the request that contain argument directed to patentability/unpatentability are included in the page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such papers include affidavits, declarations, litigation papers (briefs, trial transcripts, invalidity contentions, expert opinions). If only a portion of a paper contains argument, the entire paper counts toward the page limit. Conclusions and definitions are deemed argumentative. A page consisting solely of a signature is not included. Whether a paper contains argument is within the sole discretion of the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting exceptions for claim charts and affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim charts drafted by the requester may be single-spaced but must conform to other formatting requirements (font type/size, margins) and the page limit; affidavits/declarations drafted by the requester should conform to the formatting and page limit requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original documents not drafted by the requester, or drafted earlier for another proceeding or litigation, should not be altered or modified for submission in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-streamlined filing fee (37 CFR 1.20(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request does not meet the streamlined requirements, the filing fee in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(2) applies (a 'non-streamlined' request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include requests having greater than forty (40) pages. To be granted a filing date, a non-streamlined request must still have sufficient clarity and contrast to permit reproduction and OCR. If a requester indicates intent to submit the reduced fee but pays the higher fee, the Office will accept the paid fee and refunds may be requested if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and submission format of the patent (single-sided, double-column spec)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent copy submitted should present the specification and claims in double-column format and all pages must be plainly written on one side of paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawing pages and front page should be presented as they appear in the printed patent. A two-sided copy is not proper. Include any disclaimers, certificates of correction, or reexamination certificates as part of the patent copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet (ADS) under 37 CFR 1.76 cannot be submitted in a reexamination proceeding except as provided in MPEP § 2258.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include an ADS unless specifically permitted per MPEP guidance cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete requests: treatment and opportunity to cure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the filing fee and applicable excess claim fees are not paid in full, or the request fails to meet requirements of the governing fee rule and 37 CFR 1.510(a) and (b), the request is incomplete and generally will not be granted a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requester is usually given one opportunity to cure defects; failure to cure results in no filing date and possible placement of the papers in the patent file as a 37 CFR 1.501 submission. See MPEP § 2227 and § 2206 for handling of prior art citations or written statements under 1.501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds for denied, vacated, or incomplete requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ex parte reexamination request is subsequently denied or vacated, or is found incomplete and the defect is not cured, a refund will be made in accordance with 37 CFR 1.26 (c)(1) or (a) as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester checked the reduced-fee box but paid the higher fee, the higher fee will be accepted and the requester may file for a refund providing reasons why the request met the reduced-fee requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question of Patentability standard (MPEP § 2216)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must demonstrate a 'substantial new question of patentability' affecting any claim of the patent based on prior patents and printed publications; if such a question is found, an order for ex parte reexamination is issued (35 U.S.C. 304).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is insufficient merely to propose rejections. The requester must show a patent or printed publication relied upon in a proposed rejection presents a new, non-cumulative technological teaching not previously considered and discussed on the record during prosecution of the application (and any other prior proceeding) that resulted in the patent. Old art may raise a substantial new question only if it is presented/viewed in a new light or a different way, in view of a material new argument or interpretation. The KSR decision does not alter the legal standard for ordering reexamination; merely invoking KSR without presenting the art in a new light will not raise a substantial new question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity status statements (small/micro/large) for fee determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Different filing fees apply to large entities, small entities, and micro entities; a requester who claims small or micro entity status must affirmatively state eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requester can assert small entity status by checking the appropriate box on the transmittal form (PTO/SB/57). Only a patent owner requester can establish micro entity status; a third‑party requester cannot claim micro entity status. See 37 CFR 1.27 and 1.29 and MPEP §§ 509.02–509.04 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee schedule amounts for ex parte reexamination (37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) and (c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For streamlined requests (1.20(c)(1)) the fee amounts are: micro entity $1,260.00; small entity $2,520.00; other than small or micro entity $6,300.00. For non-streamlined requests (1.20(c)(2)) the fees are: micro entity $2,520.00; small entity $5,040.00; other than small or micro entity $12,600.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entire fee required under the applicable paragraph must be paid for a filing date to be granted. For requests filed before Jan 16, 2018, former fee rules applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity via registered practitioner and certification obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A real party in interest may remain anonymous by utilizing services of a registered practitioner; the practitioner submitting the request will certify compliance (including estoppel certification) when transacting business before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual filing on their own behalf must sign and cannot remain anonymous because the individual must sign the document including the 1.510(b)(6) certification.
